extracted.intended_audience: students, scholars, and policymakers interested in the theory and design of representative government
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting and applying normative criteria for how a representative assembly and the broader constitutional system ought to be constituted and to act (functions, composition, checks, and relations with administration). Useful for assessing institutional design, constitutional reform, or political-theory analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper office of a representative assembly (watch and control)
rubrics_metrics.description: The proper office of a representative assembly is to watch and control the government; to throw the light of publicity on its acts; to compel a full exposition and justification of all of them which any one considers questionable; to censure them if found condemnable, and, if the men who compose the government abuse their trust, or fulfill it in a manner which conflicts with the deliberate sense of the nation, to expel them from office, and either expressly or virtually appoint their successors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The assembly's powers of publicity, censure, and removal provide ample security for liberty; its task is supervision and criticism rather than the detailed conduct of government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of legislative doing from deliberation (specialized skilled legislation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Legislation should assume its proper place as a work of skilled labor and special study and experience; the fit office of an assembly is to see that individuals specially trained to govern are honestly and intelligently chosen, and to interfere no further except by suggestion and criticism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide machinery (specialized bodies/commissions) for preparing and altering bills rather than relying on a miscellaneous representative body to perform detailed legislative drafting; avoid the assembly's trying to 'do' what requires special cultivation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parliament as Committee of Grievances and Congress of Opinions (forum for public debate)
rubrics_metrics.description: Parliament should be at once the nation's Committee of Grievances and its Congress of Opinions; an arena in which not only the general opinion of the nation, but that of every section and eminent individual, can produce itself in full light and challenge discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure assemblies are open forums where every interest and shade of opinion can be passionately pleaded in the face of opponents and tested by adverse controversy; this public testing legitimizes decisions and informs government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publicity and liberty of discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: By the utmost possible publicity and liberty of discussion the whole public are made, to a certain extent, participants in the government, and sharers in the instruction and mental exercise derived from it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maximize openness and free debate so that public opinion can form, be tested, and influence government without resort to force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation as a fair sample of society
rubrics_metrics.description: Representative assemblies, when properly constituted, are a fair sample of every grade of intellect among the people which is at all entitled to a voice in public affairs; their part is to indicate wants, to be an organ for popular demands, and a place of adverse discussion for all opinions relating to public matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Composition should reflect diverse social groups and intellectual shades so that all sections find someone to speak their mind and are thereby corrected of illusions about their strength.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate mental qualifications in the controlling body
rubrics_metrics.description: A representative government is liable to positive evils from general ignorance and insufficient mental qualifications in the controlling body; the constitution of representation must secure an adequate amount of intelligence and knowledge in the representative assembly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design selection, electoral, and institutional features so that the assembly attains the mental competency needed to supervise and check the executive effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective accountability mechanisms (right to remove ministers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the constitutional right to turn ministers out of office is admitted in principle and fully operative in practice, there is no fear that the assembly will not be willing to trust its ministers with desirable power; the assembly must be able to expel them and appoint successors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure clear constitutional powers (e.g., votes of no confidence, removal mechanisms) that bind the executive to the assembly's supervision while enabling the assembly to withhold or grant support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance between popular control and skilled administration
rubrics_metrics.description: There should be a combination of the advantages of a skilled bureaucracy (trained, experienced administrators) with general control exercised by bodies representative of the people; separate the functions of control and criticism from the actual conduct of affairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide for experienced, professionally trained executives operating under strict responsibility to the nation, while preserving popular oversight and the capacity for public influence and renewal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wide diffusion of public function exercise (inclusivity of participation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The advantage lies with the form of popular government which most widely diffuses the exercise of public functions: excluding fewest from suffrage and opening to all classes the widest participation in judicial and administrative business (jury-trial, municipal offices, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote broad civic participation and access to public roles so citizens gain the instruction and mental exercise derived from government participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guarding against sinister/sectional interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Representative bodies are liable to evils from modes of action dictated by sinister interests (interests conflicting with the general welfare of the community); such sectional or class interests may produce legislation opposite to impartial regard for the community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build constitutional and institutional checks to prevent majority or influential sectional interests from enacting policies that serve their narrow advantage at the expense of general welfare (protect minority rights, prevent opportunistic taxation/spoliation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate distribution and delimitation of powers (avoid under- and over-powering)
rubrics_metrics.description: Negative defects include governments not concentrating sufficient power to fulfill necessary offices and assemblies being jealous or too lavish of power—giving wholesale authority then interfering in its exercise; avoid both under-authorizing and enabling excessive meddling by assemblies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocate powers so executive has enough authority to govern effectively while assemblies retain supervisory rights without micromanaging administration; institutionalize boundaries to prevent repeated single-act interference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preventing bureaucratic routine and pedantocracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Bureaucracy accumulates experience and skill but tends to become routine and pedantocratic, losing its vital principle and resisting improvement; a popular element is necessary to enable original talent within administration to prevail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain channels for innovation and external challenge (popular oversight, political appointment, accountability) so professional administration does not ossify into self-perpetuating routine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of long-term and distant interests (posterity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Governments and legislatures must not be guided solely by immediate and apparent interests; disinterested regard for posterity and distant interests (conscience, public spirit) must temper actions that would be advantageous only in the short term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutional design and political culture should encourage consideration of long-term consequences and the interests of future generations, resisting short-sighted or purely immediate class-driven measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit-based selection and strict responsibility of public officers
rubrics_metrics.description: The work of government should be entrusted to individuals of acquired knowledge and practiced intelligence, under strict responsibility to the nation; assemblies should ensure those individuals are honestly and intelligently chosen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design selection processes, ministerial accountability, and standards of responsibility to promote competent appointments and hold officeholders answerable for conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assemblies as instruments to reveal and marshal public opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: An assembly is a place where the opinion which prevails in the nation makes itself manifest as prevailing, and marshals its hosts in the presence of the government, enabling and compelling the government to give way to it on the mere manifestation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure assemblies function to aggregate and display public opinion clearly to government so that responsiveness can occur without force; protect mechanisms for representation and communication between public sentiment and policy.
